newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds lower, nervous about data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds lower, nervous about data.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were lower in line with Treasuries by late afternoon Friday, with discount coupons off as much as 11/32.
Traders said the market is anxious about a slew of top-tier economic data scheduled for release next week.
"Its been pretty quiet today, but I think some people are selling off in preperation for next week's (economic) numbers," said a regional trader.
"A week with producer prices, consumer prices and retail sales always plays on your nerves," he said.
By late afternoon Friday, pass-throughs were 3/32 to 11/32 lower.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 10/32 at 100-21/32, yielding 121 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper were both off 9/32 at 100-18/32 and 100-22/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was down 6/32 at 101-25/32 to yield 6.26 percent.

Producer prices for October are slated for release Wednesday, in which economists in a Reuters poll forecast a 0.2 percent rise in the overall PPI. Excluding food and energy, PPI is seen up 0.1 percent.
